---
title: "About"
description-meta: "How Canawler builds a reproducible, source-aware public dataset for the Chesapeake & Ohio Canal."
---

Canawler is a public data project about the Chesapeake & Ohio Canal: its towpath,
locks, aqueducts, campgrounds, access points, visitor amenities, and selected
canal-corridor features. It focuses on a coherent, reproducible data foundation
rather than personal progress tracking or a comprehensive railroad-history
inventory.

## Provenance

The current reference inputs draw from:

- the National Park Service Public Trails dataset for towpath geometry;
- the NPS C&O Canal Recreational Guide by Milepost for places and amenities;
- the 2026 NPS Superintendent's Compendium, approved September 10, 2026, for
  campground designations;
- the C&O Canal Association access guide for practical access locations;
- NPS and C&O Canal Trust lock references for numbering, mileposts, and names;
- the C&O Canal Trust aqueduct guide for names and mileposts;
- a transcribed historical guidebook table for aqueduct construction details.

Canawler performs normalization, deterministic ID assignment, reference matching,
linear referencing, relationship generation, and validation. Those derived facts
are identified separately from source facts in the [source registry](data/public/json/sources.json).

The data supports exploration and analysis. It is not a navigation product and
should not be treated as current trail-condition guidance.

## Licensing

Canawler's original software, documentation, and generated dataset files are
offered under the repository's
[MIT License](https://github.com/derailable/canawler/blob/main/LICENSE) to the
extent the project holds rights to them. Upstream facts and source materials
remain attributable to their providers; the
[source registry](data/public/json/sources.json) records those relationships and
the latest source checks.
